title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics in the proper sense. It is a typed page, labelled 'MA 21', that was scanned upside down and has a vertical stroke drawn across it. It appears to be a discarded draft or typescript page from Récoltes et Semailles, specifically the Mebkhout / 'Colloque Pervers' notes of L'Enterrement. It was presumably reused as scrap paper inside the July 1986 workshop notes; the neighbouring handwritten pages are about Boolean subalgebras generated by pairs b ≤ c in an ordered set Σ with a disjointness relation, and are unrelated.

Content of the page:
1. The end of a passage that weighs credit for the Riemann–Hilbert correspondence. It credits Mebkhout with three things: a precise formulation in terms of an ad hoc notion of 'regularity', which Kashiwara did not have in 1975–76; the proof, whose main ingredients were already in his thesis in the core case of D^∞-modules; and doing this at a time when the statement was felt to be marginal.
2. A nuance on the 'philosophy of Mebkhout' of D-modules. Grothendieck says Mebkhout was apparently the only one, between 1976 and 1980, devoted to developing and publicising this new 'philosophy of coefficients'. He adds that Kashiwara's role in the emergence of certain important ideas must nonetheless not be ignored, even though it was transmitted orally, as Grothendieck's own ideas often were in the 1960s.
3. Two complements, dated 6 May 1986, to a footnote on p. 963 of the Récoltes et Semailles typescript:
   - (x) Kashiwara should be removed from the list of participants in the 'mystification-escroquerie' of the Colloque Pervers (Luminy 1981). He was rather, after Mebkhout and Grothendieck himself, its main 'dindon de la farce', since he is not mentioned there either.
   - (xx) Pierre Schapira pointed out that the Fourier transform for D-modules had already been developed, though not under that name, in Sato–Kawai–Kashiwara 1973. That is well before Malgrange's work on the topic.
errors: No mathematical errors, since there is no mathematical argument on the page.

The historical priority claims are Grothendieck's partisan judgements, partly relayed from Schapira, and should be read as such. Riemann–Hilbert is usually credited jointly to Kashiwara (1980/84) and Mebkhout (1980/84).

The Fourier-transform remark refers to the quantized contact transformations / microlocal machinery of SKK 1973. Identifying this with the Fourier transform for D-modules (Brylinski–Malgrange–Verdier, Malgrange) is a loose but common observation.

ideas.what: Riemann–Hilbert correspondence for regular holonomic D-modules; credit to Mebkhout for the formulation via a notion of regularity and for a proof rooted in his D^∞-module thesis
ideas.where_published: Récoltes et Semailles (L'Enterrement, notes on Mebkhout and the Colloque Pervers)

ideas.what: Mebkhout's 'philosophy of coefficients' via D-modules, as a counterpart of Grothendieck's six-operations / coefficients philosophy
ideas.modern_name: D-modules as coefficients; perverse sheaves and the de Rham functor

missed.claim: These are dated addenda (6 May 1986) to a Récoltes et Semailles footnote: they withdraw Kashiwara from the 'Colloque Pervers' accusation and relay Schapira's attribution of the D-module Fourier transform to SKK 1973. If they are absent from the distributed versions of Récoltes et Semailles, they are a minor historical correction to the record.
missed.quote: Il y a lieu, visiblement, d'exclure le nom de M. Kashiwara de la liste des participants à la "mystification-escroquerie" du Colloque Pervers
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of interest only to historians of the Riemann–Hilbert priority dispute. It is not mathematically new.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a reused typescript fragment of Récoltes et Semailles about credit for Riemann–Hilbert and D-modules. Its content is well known in substance; the only possibly unrecorded items are the dated 6 May 1986 addenda about Kashiwara and Schapira's Fourier-transform remark.
transcription_corrections: The page image is upside down. It is a typed page ('MA 21') with a vertical line across it, unrelated to the handwritten lattice and Boolean-algebra notes on the neighbouring pages.
'quand par la suite il s'arrivera de parler' should read 'quand par la suite il m'arrivera de parler'.
Above 'Page 963' there is a struck-out 'xxxx'. The line before it is a long crossed-out typed passage, essentially illegible.

'au développement' is the reading at the end of line 3 of the second paragraph. The phrase transcribed '[-...-] en train de naître sans-crier-gare' is uncertain: the image shows struck typing ('xxxx') after 'coéfficients'. The words 'sans-crier-gare' may be a misreading of a word split across lines ('su-/jet' belongs to 'à ce sujet').
In (x), the struck-out word after 'à part Mebkhout' is a crossed-out 'xxexpériences'-like overstrike, not content.
